title: OpenAI and Anthropic Engage in Price War as Chinese AI Rivals Gain Market Traction
summary: Leading US AI companies OpenAI and Anthropic are reducing prices for their mid-tier AI models to retain cost-sensitive customers amid competition from cheaper, high-performance Chinese alternatives like Moonshot and DeepSeek. The price cuts, such as OpenAI's 80% reduction for GPT-5.6 Luna and Anthropic's launch of Claude Opus 5 at half the price of its flagship model, reflect a shift toward usage-based billing and cost efficiency. Chinese AI models, often open-source, are narrowing the performance gap, prompting concerns in the US tech industry about losing market share despite heavy investments in maintaining technological leadership.
key_points: OpenAI and Anthropic are slashing prices for mid-tier AI models (e.g., OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Luna reduced by 80%) to compete with cheaper Chinese alternatives.
Chinese AI developers like Moonshot and DeepSeek are gaining traction with open, customizable models that challenge US dominance in performance and cost.
Usage-based billing is replacing flat subscriptions, increasing cost pressures on corporate AI users, leading some (e.g., DoorDash, Airbnb) to adopt Chinese models.
Token pricing varies by model and effort settings, complicating direct cost comparisons; more capable models may use fewer tokens, reducing overall expenses.
Anthropic’s Opus 5 and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Luna are priced competitively against Chinese models like Moonshot’s Kimi K3 and DeepSeek’s V4 Flash, though US models remain pricier per task in some cases.
US AI labs are focusing on defending their premium models while cutting prices for mid-tier offerings, signaling a strategic shift in response to market competition.
The price war coincides with OpenAI and Anthropic’s plans for IPOs, with investors scrutinizing the industry’s ability to generate returns amid high spending.
